# 1 Samuel Chapter 20 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 162r-162v | **Source Image:** 1SA_020_page_001.jpg, 1SA_020_page_002.jpg, 1SA_020_page_003.jpg

---

**20:1** And-David-fled from-Naioth in-Ramah, and-came and-said before Jonathan, "What have-I-done? What [is] my-iniquity, and-what [is] my-sin before your-father, that he-[is]-seeking my-life [nefesh]?"

**20:2** And-he-said to-him, "Far-be-it [chalilah]! You-shall-not die. Behold, my-father does-not do [a]-great thing or [a]-small thing without-uncovering my-ear. And-why should-my-father-hide from-me this thing? This [is] not [so]."

**20:3** And-David-swore again and-said, "Your-father surely-knows that I-have-found favor in-your-eyes, and-he-said, 'Let-not Jonathan know this, lest he-be-grieved.' But-truly, [as]-YHWH lives and-[as]-your-soul [nefesh] lives, for-as-a-step [kefesaʿ] [between] me and-between death."

**20:4** And-Jonathan-said to David, "Whatever your-soul [nefesh] says, I-will-do [it] for-you."

**20:5** And-David-said to Jonathan, "Behold, tomorrow [is the]-new-moon [chodesh], and-I surely should-be-sitting with the-king to-eat. And-you-shall-send-me-away, and-I-will-hide in-the-field until the-evening of-the-third [day].

**20:6** If your-father-misses me at-all, then-you-shall-say, 'David earnestly-asked of-me to-run to Beth-lehem his-city, for [the]-sacrifice of-the-days [is there] for-all the-clan [mishpachah].'

**20:7** If thus he-says, 'Good' -- peace [shalom] to-your-servant. But-if it-is-hot [to]-anger to-him, know that the-evil is-determined from-with-him.

**20:8** And-you-shall-do loyal-love [chesed] with your-servant, for into-a-covenant of-YHWH you-have-brought your-servant with-you. And-if there-is in-me iniquity, put-me-to-death yourself; and-unto your-father, why [would] you-bring-me?"

**20:9** And-Jonathan-said, "Far-be-it [chalilah] from-you! For if I-surely-knew that the-evil is-determined from-with my-father to-come upon-you, would-I-not tell it to-you?"

**20:10** And-David-said to Jonathan, "Who will-tell me, or what [if] your-father-answers you [something]-hard?"

**20:11** And-Jonathan-said to David, "Come, and-let-us-go-out to-the-field." And-they-both-went-out to-the-field.

**20:12** And-Jonathan-said to David, "YHWH, God of-Israel -- when I-sound-out my-father about-this-time tomorrow [or] the-third [day], and-behold, [there is]-good toward David, and-I-do-not then send to-you and-uncover your-ear --

**20:13** thus may-YHWH-do to-Jonathan and-thus may-He-add. But-if the-evil is-good-to my-father [i.e., he intends evil] against-you, then-I-will-uncover your-ear, and-send-you-away, and-you-shall-go in-peace [shalom]. And-may-YHWH be with-you as He-was with my-father.

**20:14** And-not-only -- if I [am]-yet alive, and-you-shall-do with-me [the]-loyal-love [chesed] of-YHWH, and-I-shall-not die.

**20:15** And-you-shall-not cut-off your-loyal-love [chesed] from-with my-house forever [ʿad ʿolam], and-not when-YHWH cuts-off the-enemies of-David, each from-upon [the]-face of-the-ground."

**20:16** And-Jonathan-cut [a covenant] with [the]-house of-David, [saying], "And-YHWH-shall-require [it] from-[the]-hand of-[the]-enemies of-David."

**20:17** And-Jonathan-continued to-swear to-David, because-of-his-love for-him, for with-[the]-love of-his-soul [nefesh] he-loved-him.

**20:18** And-Jonathan-said to-him, "Tomorrow [is the]-new-moon [chodesh], and-you-will-be-missed, for your-seat will-be-empty.

**20:19** And-on-the-third-day you-shall-go-down quickly and-come to the-place where you-hid-yourself on-the-day of-the-deed, and-you-shall-sit beside the-stone Ezel.

**20:20** And-I will-shoot three arrows to-its-side, sending for-myself at-a-target.

**20:21** And-behold, I-will-send the-lad, [saying], 'Go, find the-arrows.' If I-surely-say to-the-lad, 'Behold, the-arrows [are] on-this-side-of-you, take-them' -- then-come, for [there is]-peace [shalom] for-you and-nothing [is wrong], [as]-YHWH lives.

**20:22** But-if thus I-say to-the-youth, 'Behold, the-arrows [are] beyond-you' -- go, for YHWH has-sent-you-away.

**20:23** And-the-word that we-spoke, I and-you -- behold, YHWH [is] between-me and-between-you forever [ʿad ʿolam]."

**20:24** And-David-hid in-the-field. And-the-new-moon [chodesh] came, and-the-king-sat at the-meal [literally: the-bread] to-eat.

**20:25** And-the-king-sat upon his-seat as-time-by-time [kepha'am bepha'am], upon [the]-seat by-the-wall. And-Jonathan-arose, and-Abner-sat at-[the]-side of-Saul, and-David's-place was-empty.

**20:26** And-Saul did-not speak anything on-that day, for he-said, "[It is a]-chance [miqreh]; he [is] not clean, for he-has-not-been-cleansed."

**20:27** And-it-was on-the-morrow of-the-new-moon, the-second [day], and-David's-place was-empty. And-Saul-said to Jonathan his-son, "Why has-not-come [the]-son of-Jesse, both yesterday and-today, to the-meal [literally: the-bread]?"

**20:28** And-Jonathan-answered Saul, "David earnestly-asked from-with-me [to go] to Beth-lehem.

**20:29** And-he-said, 'Send-me-away, please, for [a]-clan sacrifice [is] for-us in-the-city, and-my-brother himself has-commanded me. And-now, if I-have-found favor in-your-eyes, let-me-slip-away, please, and-see my-brothers.' Therefore he-has-not come to the-table of-the-king."

**20:30** And-[the]-anger of-Saul was-hot against-Jonathan, and-he-said to-him, "Son of-a-perverse rebellious-[woman] [ben naʿavat hammardut]! Do-I-not know that you [are]-choosing [the]-son of-Jesse to-your-shame and-to-[the]-shame of-[the]-nakedness of-your-mother?

**20:31** For all the-days that [the]-son of-Jesse [is]-alive upon the-ground, you-shall-not-be-established, you and-your-kingdom. And-now, send and-take him to-me, for he [is a]-son of-death [ben mavet]."

**20:32** And-Jonathan-answered Saul his-father, and-said to-him, "Why should-he-be-put-to-death? What has-he-done?"

**20:33** And-Saul-hurled the-spear at-him to-strike-him. And-Jonathan-knew that it [was]-determined from-with his-father to-put-David-to-death.

**20:34** And-Jonathan-arose from-the-table in-burning anger [chori af], and-did-not eat bread on-[the]-second day of-the-new-moon, for he-was-grieved concerning David, for his-father had-humiliated-him.

**20:35** And-it-was in-the-morning, and-Jonathan-went-out to-the-field for-[the]-appointment [of]-David, and-a-small lad [was] with-him.

**20:36** And-he-said to-his-lad, "Run, find, please, the-arrows that I [am]-shooting." The-lad ran, and-he shot the-arrow to-pass-beyond-him.

**20:37** And-the-lad-came unto [the]-place of-the-arrow that Jonathan had-shot, and-Jonathan-called after the-lad and-said, "Is-not the-arrow beyond-you?"

**20:38** And-Jonathan-called after the-lad, "Hurry, make-haste, do-not stand!" And-[the]-lad of-Jonathan gathered the-arrows and-came to his-master.

**20:39** And-the-lad did-not know anything; only Jonathan and-David knew the-matter.

**20:40** And-Jonathan-gave his-weapons to the-lad that [was]-his, and-said to-him, "Go, bring [them] to-the-city."

**20:41** The-lad went, and-David arose from-beside the-south-[side], and-fell on-his-face to-the-ground, and-bowed-down three times. And-they-kissed each-other and-they-wept each with-the-other, until David-made-great [i.e., wept greatly].

**20:42** And-Jonathan-said to-David, "Go in-peace [shalom], [in]-that which we-have-sworn, [the]-two of-us, in-[the]-name of-YHWH, saying, 'YHWH shall-be between-me and-between-you, and-between my-seed and-between your-seed, forever [ʿad ʿolam].'" And-he-arose and-went, and-Jonathan came to-the-city.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **20:3 -- "as-a-step"** (kefesaʿ): Literally "as a step/pace." David says there is but a single step between him and death -- a vivid spatial metaphor for his mortal peril.

2. **20:5 -- chodesh**: The new moon, marking the first day of the lunar month. It was observed as a feast day with sacrificial meals (cf. Num 28:11-15). The new-moon meal at Saul's table was a fixed obligation of the royal court.

3. **20:19 -- "the stone Ezel"** (haʾeven haʾazel): The Leningrad Codex reads ha'azel. The meaning is debated -- possibly "the stone of departure" (from ʾazal, "to go away") or a proper name. Some read "the stone Ezel" as a known landmark.

4. **20:25 -- Textual note**: The Leningrad Codex reads vayyaqom Yehonatan, "and Jonathan arose." LXX reads "and Jonathan sat" (proephthase), which would make better narrative sense for a meal scene. The MT is the more difficult reading and is retained.

5. **20:30 -- "son of a perverse rebellious woman"** (ben naʿavat hammardut): This is among the most vicious insults in the Hebrew Bible. Saul attacks Jonathan by insulting his mother -- literally "son of the perversity of rebellion." The phrase defies smooth translation; it implies Jonathan's loyalty to David is as shameful and twisted as sexual deviance.

6. **20:41 -- "until David made great"** (ʿad David higdil): The Leningrad Codex has higdil (hiphil of gadal, "to make great"). This likely means "David wept the most" or "David exceeded [in weeping]." Some emend to higdil [bekhi], supplying "weeping." The Ketiv/Qere traditions preserve this enigmatic form.

7. **20:42 -- Verse division**: In some traditions (including MT Leningrad), the final clause "And-he-arose and-went, and-Jonathan came to-the-city" is numbered as 21:1 (Hebrew). English versification follows the chapter division that places 42 verses in ch. 20.
